nodes.title: Trade in the spotlight: enhancing gravity model predictions with nightlights and population-weighted distance measures
nodes.label: Trade in the spotlight (2025)
nodes.desc: A geodesic distance between population-weighted centroids, built from VIIRS nightlights and gridded population, measurably improves gravity-model fit.

meta.question: Does a gravity model fit better when bilateral distance reflects where population and measured economic activity are located within countries?
meta.limit: The preprint does not establish the planned panel, transport-network extension, or structural-gravity validation; those remain development work with no completed results.

nodes.title: Effective distance: a satellite-calibrated bilateral trade-cost panel, 2000-2024
nodes.label: Effective-distance panel
nodes.desc: A planned 2000-2024 panel of bilateral effective distance from nightlights, gridded population, and transport networks; no results yet.

meta.question: Can a time-varying measure of bilateral effective distance represent changes in population, economic activity, infrastructure, and transport corridors?
meta.limit: No completed results, validated panel, coverage claim, or public data release exists yet.

nodes.title: Occlusion and adaptation: a closed-loop spatial-labor model of Ukraine's wartime economic reorganization, 2022-2025
nodes.label: Ukraine occlusion model
nodes.desc: A proposed measurement program for Ukraine's wartime economic activity using administrative, satellite, maritime, and labor data; no results yet.

meta.question: How has Ukraine's wartime economic activity reorganized across space when official measurement is itself disrupted by conflict, occupation, and displacement?
meta.role: Coauthor with Elizaveta Gonchar; contribution statement pending joint ratification
meta.limit: No completed results, index, or ratified contribution statement exists yet.

nodes.title: Redefining Trade Dynamics: Incorporating Network Centrality, Spatial Heterogeneity, and Optimal Transport Theory into Models of International Trade
nodes.label: Dissertation (2024)
nodes.desc: Georgia Tech doctoral dissertation on network centrality in gravity models, population-weighted bilateral distance, and optimal transport in trade.

meta.question: How do network position, within-country spatial heterogeneity, and optimal transport change the representation of international trade?
meta.limit: This record covers the three chapters of the 2024 dissertation. Later papers and datasets that build on them have their own records and statuses.

nodes.title: A unifying framework for economic equilibrium and optimal transport in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces
nodes.label: Equilibrium and optimal transport
nodes.desc: A theoretical working paper connecting economic equilibrium and optimal transport when the economic object is a function or distribution.

meta.question: Under what conditions can economic equilibrium be represented as an optimal-transport problem in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space?
meta.limit: This record states the paper's question and approach; the theorem statements and their assumptions are in the SSRN manuscript.

nodes.title: Human or Machine? Out-of-Time Validation of Task-Level AI Exposure Ratings
nodes.label: Human or Machine? Out-of-Time Validation of Task-Level AI Exposure Ratings
nodes.desc: A paper in progress testing human and GPT-4 task-level AI-exposure ratings against measures of task use published after the ratings were made.

meta.question: Which task-level AI-exposure ratings continue to align with public measures of task use that appeared after the ratings were constructed?
meta.limit: The paper is in progress and reports no results yet.

nodes.title: The rural mobilization gap in a U.S. place-based tax credit
nodes.label: NMTC rural gap (2026)
nodes.desc: In the New Markets Tax Credit, the raw rural leverage gap of −0.262 falls to −0.047 within the same Community Development Entity; descriptive, noncausal.

meta.question: Does the rural private-leverage gap persist when rural and urban projects are compared within the same Community Development Entity?
meta.role: Sole author; Katia Antunes and Elizaveta Gonchar are acknowledged contributors
meta.limit: The design is descriptive and noncausal, does not identify why intermediaries differ, and leaves the mechanism unresolved.

nodes.title: Penumbra: closed-loop observation under measurement gaps in cross-border trade
nodes.label: Penumbra
nodes.desc: A theory paper in progress on measuring cross-border trade when the act of observing that trade changes what becomes visible.

meta.question: How should a trade model represent settings where the equilibrium changes the observation system used to measure that equilibrium?
meta.limit: The paper is in progress and reports no results yet.

nodes.title: Empirical observation equilibria: the Russian seaborne-crude corridor, 2021-2024
nodes.label: Russian seaborne crude
nodes.desc: A proposed design using AIS tracks, port arrivals, and commodity-flow records to study Russian seaborne crude under sanctions; no results yet.

meta.question: Can public shipping and port records identify the feedback between sanctions-evasion behavior and the observation system used to measure Russian seaborne crude?
meta.limit: No empirical results exist yet; identification, coverage, and data construction remain under development.

nodes.title: AI and the Entry-Level Labor Market
nodes.label: AI and entry-level labor
nodes.desc: An empirical design asking whether early-career employment changed differently in occupations with greater generative-AI exposure; no results yet.

meta.question: Did early-career employment change differently after widespread generative-AI adoption in occupations with greater measured AI exposure?
meta.limit: No empirical results exist yet; the public record describes a design and planned analysis only.

nodes.title: Lecture summaries
nodes.label: Lecture summaries
nodes.desc: One-page summaries of the fifteen lectures: the economic question, the central relation, an individual problem with a worked answer, a consequential failure, and its repair.

nodes.title: Lecture 1 summary: The decision and its information set
nodes.label: Lecture 1 summary: The decision and its information set
nodes.desc: Define an economic target and decision deadline before choosing a model. A low error cannot rescue information unavailable at the origin.

nodes.title: Lecture 2 summary: Persistence, recursion, and aggregation
nodes.label: Lecture 2 summary: Persistence, recursion, and aggregation
nodes.desc: Persistence carries an earlier deviation forward. The intercept is an increment in the recursion; it is not generally the long-run mean.

nodes.title: Lecture 3 summary: ARMA models and recoverable innovations
nodes.label: Lecture 3 summary: ARMA models and recoverable innovations
nodes.desc: Observed memory can arise in the level recursion and the innovation sequence. Stationarity and invertibility answer different questions.

nodes.title: Lecture 4 summary: Forecasts that survive a chronological comparison
nodes.label: Lecture 4 summary: Forecasts that survive a chronological comparison
nodes.desc: An equation is only part of a forecasting algorithm. Windows, horizons, refits, releases, and fallbacks determine its feasible behavior.

nodes.title: Lecture 5 summary: Signals, noisy measures, and information-preserving filters
nodes.label: Lecture 5 summary: Signals, noisy measures, and information-preserving filters
nodes.desc: An indicator measures an economic quantity. A smooth retrospective graph can use observations unavailable when a real-time decision was made.

nodes.title: Lecture 6 summary: Trends, unit roots, and misleading level regressions
nodes.label: Lecture 6 summary: Trends, unit roots, and misleading level regressions
nodes.desc: A deterministic trend with temporary deviations differs from a stochastic trend with permanent innovations. Their variances and testing references differ.

nodes.title: Lecture 7 summary: Weather, seasonality, and dynamic regression
nodes.label: Lecture 7 summary: Weather, seasonality, and dynamic regression
nodes.desc: Economic predictors can explain demand while the residual remains dynamic. A feasible forecast must specify the future predictor path.

nodes.title: Lecture 8 summary: Estimating a latent state as observations arrive
nodes.label: Lecture 8 summary: Estimating a latent state as observations arrive
nodes.desc: A latent state and its indicator follow separate equations. The Kalman gain weights an observation by its uncertainty relative to the predicted state.

nodes.title: Lecture 9 summary: Multivariate dynamics and regional networks
nodes.label: Lecture 9 summary: Multivariate dynamics and regional networks
nodes.desc: Several outcomes evolve together through a matrix recursion. Stability belongs to the system, and predictive cross-lags do not themselves identify transmission.

nodes.title: Lecture 10 summary: What an impulse response can claim
nodes.label: Lecture 10 summary: What an impulse response can claim
nodes.desc: Reduced-form covariance does not uniquely determine economic shocks. A covariance-preserving rotation changes the impact pattern while retaining observable second moments.

nodes.title: Lecture 11 summary: A stable relation between moving levels
nodes.label: Lecture 11 summary: A stable relation between moving levels
nodes.desc: Moving levels can share a stationary spread. The long-run relation and short-run adjustment are distinct, and a change forecast must be returned to the current level.

nodes.title: Lecture 12 summary: Predictable risk with an unpredictable return
nodes.label: Lecture 12 summary: Predictable risk with an unpredictable return
nodes.desc: A zero predictable mean can coexist with predictable risk. A variance recursion does not establish mean-return predictability, and a tail quantile needs a distribution.

nodes.title: Lecture 13 summary: When the model or the measurement changes
nodes.label: Lecture 13 summary: When the model or the measurement changes
nodes.desc: A model has a period of usefulness. Shorter windows can adapt to change while sacrificing precision; neither window policy wins under every mechanism.

nodes.title: Lecture 14 summary: Freeze a revision before its next test
nodes.label: Lecture 14 summary: Freeze a revision before its next test
nodes.desc: A revision is a new empirical argument. Its selection record, update rule, fallback, and untouched next comparison must be preserved together.

nodes.label: Lecture 15 summary: Defend a forecast in an unfamiliar setting
nodes.desc: Transfer the argument, not its assumptions automatically. An unfamiliar regional financial setting still requires a target, information clock, dynamics, uncertainty, and defensible action.
